value.option_title: Reconcile the GISMo Hit@1 discrepancy across the two protocols before any width sweep
value.question: Does widening a graph ingredient-substitution ranker raise its Hit@1 on Recipe1MSubs, once the 20.56 vs 34.53 baseline gap between two GISMo protocols is explained?
value.hypothesis: Hit@1 saturates by width 300 because GISMo already ranks 6,653 ingredients with a small GNN; more width won't help [s1].
held_fixed: candidate set = full vocabulary minus source ingredient
width=300 anchor run reproduced in phase A

predictions.if_lever: Hit@1 climbs with width, at least +1 point from 300 to 512, showing ranker capacity is the lever.
predictions.if_not: Hit@1 is flat from 300 to 512 (within seed noise), so added width does not improve substitution ranking.
predictions.decision_rule: Compute mean Hit@1 over 5 seeds at width 512 and at width 300 (the phase-A anchor); if_lever if mean(512) - mean(300) >= +1.0 point, else if_not.
predictions.noise_rule: 5 seeds per width; a real gap must exceed 2x the pooled per-width std (source paper run std is 0.14 pt [s1]); smaller gaps are treated as seed noise.
predictions.expected_why: The source paper tuned width over 200-600 and kept 300, implying the ranking does not improve with more width [s1].

value.compute_tested_why: Width is the ranker-capacity lever: each level is a different model capacity, wider models cost more compute per step, and the sweep asks whether that added capacity raises Hit@1.
value.scored_against: The measured Hit@1 at width 300 must match Meta's published 20.56 (within ±0.5 pt) before the width trend is trusted; the trend is compared against the paper's choice of 300 over widths 400-600 [s1].

arms.what: Meta's official GISMo: full 6,653-vocab candidate set, standard 49,044/10,729/10,747 splits, merge_dict preprocessing
Rita et al. protocol: their preprocessing/candidate set/split that yields Hit@1 34.53

baseline.what: Meta GISMo published test Hit@1 on Recipe1MSubs

anchor.what: Reproduce Meta's Hit@1 20.56±0.14 [s1] with official code and data; independent 20.4 [s11].
anchor.independent_code: CEUR-WS independent GISMo reproduction reports Hits@1 20.4 on Recipe1MSubs

checks: Official GISMo hyperparameters reproduce Hit@1 = 20.56±0.14 within ±0.5 pt before anything else runs.
Rita protocol reproduces 34.53±0.10 to confirm the gap is protocol, not an implementation bug.
The isolation grid changes one knob at a time (candidate set, split, preprocessing) and attributes the 20.56→34.53 gap to one knob.
The width=300 run inside the sweep matches the phase-A reproduction within seed noise.
The official repo is pinned to PyTorch 1.7 + CUDA 10.2 + DGL 0.7; the harness ports GISMo to a modern stack and validates it against the official numbers.

phases.what: Set up the modern-PyTorch/DGL port of GISMo, download FlavorGraph nodes/edges, the GISMo substitution pickles and merge_dict, train Meta GISMo (hidden=300, emb_d=300) for 5 seeds and evaluate Hit@1.
phases.stop_rule: Stop when 5 seeds complete and test Hit@1 is reported.

gate.else: Meta's 20.56 was not reproduced within 0.5 pt; fix environment, DGL version, or data mapping before running the sweep.

phases.what: Re-run the Rita et al. protocol (their split/preprocessing/candidate set) for 5 seeds to reproduce 34.53, then change one knob at a time (candidate set, split, preprocessing) to isolate the 20.56→34.53 gap.
phases.stop_rule: Stop when the gap is attributed to one knob or 6 isolation runs are done.

gate.else: Rita's 34.53 was not reproduced; proceed with the Meta protocol only and record Rita's number as un-reproduced.

phases.what: Sweep width 64/128/256/512 x 5 seeds under the reproducing protocol, then repeat under the other protocol to report the width trend under both.
phases.stop_rule: Timer: 3 node-hours on the 8-V100 node, or all 40 runs complete, whichever comes first.

gate.else: A single run is far slower than the 0.5 h budget; do not launch the 40-run sweep, cut widths to {64,512} and re-cost.

restructuring.sequential_part: The width sweep waits on reconciliation: reproduce Meta 20.56, then Rita 34.53, then sweep — three ordered steps.

scope_gap: Shows general substitution Hit@1, not sustainability-specific substitutes; Recipe1MSubs is unlabeled for sustainability, so 'sustainable replacements' is only indirectly tested.

novelty.closest_prior: Meta's GISMo paper tuned width over 200-600 and kept 300, the largest width on this axis, but reported no width trend [s1].
novelty.left_open: No published result reports how Hit@1 changes with ranker width 64-512 on Recipe1MSubs, under either protocol.

limits: Shows general substitution Hit@1, not sustainability-specific substitutes; Recipe1MSubs is unlabeled for sustainability, so 'sustainable replacements' is only indirectly tested.
value.test_summary: Run Meta's official GISMo and Rita et al.'s protocol in one harness to reproduce 20.56 and 34.53, isolate the difference; then sweep width 64-512 at 5 seeds under the reproducing protocol and report both.
